reviews.title: Turn the volume down
reviews.text: The sound is louder than other noises on my iPhone. And there’s no way I can find to change that without changing my phone settings every time I use the app. Really hard for someone with sensory issues.

reviews.title: Great app just don’t subscribe
reviews.text:
I’ve had this app now for maybe 509 days. Started out great. But now, some of these clothes are not showing up. I emailed twice for a generic response about sending pics.  New themes start before I get all the furniture for them. It’s taking weeks to complete a set up. Just ridiculous now. I do not recommend subscribing.

reviews.title: It’s hard to add people
reviews.text:
It’s hard to add people that give you a big hug to pick you up when you’re feeling down. It’s hard to make new friends, which should be a good thing to encourage.
And I’ve also asked for someone to sponsor my daughter’s app and mine so we had Finch plus and nobody ever gets back to you. They just ignore you.
But overall, the app has helped my daughter and I get out of our depression a little bit and look forward to something or to be productive

reviews.title: Can’t get all rewards on plus
reviews.text:
I’ve missed two days on last two monthly rewards in Finch, not sure if I missed days but I’m sure I do it every day and considering I pay plus and thought you could get the prizes for 14 days after regardless this isn’t a good look at all and I’m going to be cancelling my plus so it doesn’t renew!
Ridiculous I’m not getting what I paid for!

Also, for something meant to help your mental health it’s stressful! Now all I do is box ticking before bed! I really hate these apps with streaks and after my year I will delete it tbh! I was about to delete it when I got a month free from a guardian and then felt cool as claimed all the Supergirl rewards but now it’s stressful! What’s the point when you can just tick the boxes anyways?

And I saw someone say about their bad hiring processes and that’s also very off-putting getting folks to do unpaid work. 

I don’t think any of these apps should have streaks either.

reviews.title: It was great until …
reviews.text: This app really made a difference for me and I had collected all the items. Until my data was corrupted despite having a backup. So I lost everything and their only solution was to start again with only 5000 rainbow coins! What a joke and such a blow to my mental health. They really need to make the backup system robust!

reviews.title: A Cute Idea That Tries a Bit Too Hard
reviews.text:
Finch clearly comes from a good place. The idea of pairing self-care with a little virtual pet is charming on paper, and it’s easy to see why it appeals to some people. Unfortunately, in practice the app leans so hard into “cute” that it becomes twee to the point of being almost condescending.

Everything about Finch — the language, the animations, the tone of encouragement — feels more like it’s aimed at children than adults. Tasks are framed with excessive cheerfulness and overly simplified affirmations, which can make genuine self-reflection feel trivialised. Instead of feeling supported, I often felt talked down to, as though complex emotional states could be fixed with a sticker, a smiley face, and a cartoon bird telling me I’d done great.

For people who already find self-care difficult or awkward, this kind of presentation can be actively off-putting. Rather than lowering the barrier to entry, the saccharine tone risks pushing people away entirely — reinforcing the idea that self-care is fluffy, shallow, or not meant to be taken seriously. Ironically, it’s exactly the sort of approach that can make people bounce off self-care rather than embrace it.

Finch will undoubtedly work well for some users, especially those who enjoy gamified positivity and a very gentle, childlike aesthetic. But for adults looking for something that treats their mental health with a bit more nuance, maturity, and respect, the app may feel more patronising than helpful.
